native_result.query: In what centuries did we see the highest growth phase of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: Between 1500 BCE and 1300 BCE, highest growth of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE is seen.
native_result.HypoB: The highest growth phase within 2000-1100 BCE is centered on the 15th century BCE (c. 1500-1401 BCE), with strong growth continuing through the 14th century BCE (c. 1400-1301 BCE). This is supported by three independent proxies: (1) the archaeological KDE growth rate g_all_mean peaks in the 1500s (+0.0028/yr mean, 100% positive years; top years 1432-1452 BCE) with the 1400s second (+0.0015/yr) versus negative 13th-12th centuries BCE; (2) pollen openness (100-yr smoothed) rises most strongly in the 1500s (+0.98 level, ~+2.6%/yr) and 1400s (+0.66), recovering from a 16th-century BCE trough (-1.65); (3) the four capitals (approved mapping) show the largest century gain between the 1500 and 1400 BCE markers (total mean column-delta +2.6, chiefly social +1.53 and symbolic +0.75), with wealth levels peaking at the 1400 BCE marker. Both binning schemes agree; the growth phase is bounded by the 16th-century decline and the 13th-12th century downturn.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load and clean three CSV files (capital and pollen columns use comma decimals; CE=-BCE, calBP=1950-CE verified). 2) Restrict to CE in [-2000,-1100] (901 gap-free annual points; capital has 10 discrete century markers). 3) Build century blocks by CE-flooring (Scheme A: 9 full centuries 2000s..1200s + endpoint year 1100 BCE), and Scheme B: 10 discrete points (intervals between consecutive markers). 4) Compute per-century growth proxies: mean g_all_mean (KDE growth rate), self-computed pollen-openness growth (pollen_inter / pollen_inter_100 rolling-100 means), and capital century deltas grouped into Symbolic/Social/Economic/Cultural with the approved column mapping. 5) Rank centuries per proxy, cross-validate (Spearman), and check scheme A vs B agreement; flag pollen_grate_100 as low-confidence (definition not reproducible). 6) Synthesize the highest-growth centuries and write the data-grounded English hypothesis with stated caveats.
